- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast horizons, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce next 3–5 periods by 2–5% from peak).
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias; dampen forecast variance by smoothing with 3-period moving average.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, model should anticipate pullback; add 1–2% downward adjustment in next 5–7 periods.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overweights recent history; reduce weight of last 3–5 days in forecasting if no sentiment change.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to recognize it; add a “reversal trigger” rule: if forecast > 10% above recent high, reduce next period by 3–5% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
